purpose: Manifest of reproducible cross-language fixtures for the C++ migration. No audio, model, or user data is embedded in this manifest.
materializationPolicy: Create only license-safe, deterministic fixtures; record checksums and generation commands before marking a fixture ready.

fixtures.expected: Decision: numeric enum values are accepted, normalized to the canonical camelCase name on the next save and reported with a warning; an invalid enum string falls back to defaults. C# reference behaviour verified on this file: JsonStringEnumConverter throws JsonException on the invalid string, SettingsService.Load catches it and returns new AppSettings(), so the fallback is document-wide. The file holds numeric recordingMode=1, transcriptionEngine=1, parakeetModelSize=2 and the invalid string modelSize='colossal', while every other field is non-default, so a document-wide fallback is observable. C++ assertions: all 21 fields equal the defaults, and the diagnostics report the three numeric-valued enums as warnings plus modelSize as an invalid-enum error - the C# reference has no warning channel, so that assertion is C++-only.

Deterministic 440 Hz PCM16 mono 44.1 kHz sine, 1 second; output 16 kHz mono PCM16 WAV.

materialized.format: canonical 44-byte-header RIFF/WAVE PCM16: audioFormat=1, channels=1, sampleRate=44100, bitsPerSample=16, blockAlign=2, byteRate=88200, 44100 frames (1.000 s), 88200 data bytes
materialized.expectedOutcome: Per ConvertTo16KHzMonoWav_FromMono44K_Returns16KHzMono16Bit (derived by reading the C# sources, NOT executed by .NET): 16000 Hz mono PCM16, TotalTime in [0.95, 1.05] s. The tone has no inactive frames, so SilenceTrimmer keeps every sample and the duration is preserved.
materialized.synthesisNotes: Samples are trunc(sin(2*pi*440*i/44100) * 16383.5), which is literally WavBuilderTests.GenerateSinePcm16: (short)(Math.Sin(2*PI*440*i/sr) * short.MaxValue * 0.5) with short.MaxValue=32767. Truncation toward zero matches the C# (short) cast.
materialized.notCovered: Sample values are bit-comparable with a C# run but are NOT guaranteed bit-identical to System.Math.Sin, whose libm has no specified accuracy. The generator therefore avoids math.sin entirely (see generator docstring) and computes the tone in decimal.Decimal.

fixtures.expected: Deterministic 440 Hz PCM16 stereo 48 kHz sine, 0.5 second; downmix/resample output format and duration.

materialized.format: canonical 44-byte-header RIFF/WAVE PCM16: audioFormat=1, channels=2, sampleRate=48000, bitsPerSample=16, blockAlign=4, byteRate=192000, 24000 frames (0.500 s), 96000 data bytes
materialized.expectedOutcome: Per ConvertTo16KHzMonoWav_FromStereo48K_ReturnsMono16KHz and ConvertTo16KHzMonoFloats_LengthMatchesDuration (read, NOT executed): 16000 Hz mono PCM16, TotalTime in [0.45, 0.55] s, float count in [7200, 8800].
materialized.synthesisNotes: Interleaved L,R with the identical value in both channels, so NAudio's StereoToMonoSampleProvider average is the identity and a C++ downmix that averages is directly comparable. Same 16383.5 scaling as wav-sine-44k-mono.
materialized.notCovered: A phase-offset or unequal-channel stereo case (where the downmix is not the identity) has no fixture; the manifest's hotkey/WAV contract covers only the average path.

fixtures.expected: Leading/trailing silence and quiet speech survive adaptive trim.

materialized.format: canonical 44-byte-header RIFF/WAVE PCM16: audioFormat=1, channels=1, sampleRate=16000, bitsPerSample=16, blockAlign=2, byteRate=32000, 32000 frames (2.000 s); 0.5 s exact zeros + 1.0 s of 440 Hz tone at amplitude 0.5 + 0.5 s exact zeros
materialized.expectedOutcome: Per Trim_RemovesLeadingAndTrailingSilence (read, NOT executed): trimming keeps samples [4000, 28000) = 24000 samples = exactly 1.500 s (1.0 s of speech plus the 0.25 s MarginSeconds on each side); the C# test asserts [1.4, 1.6] s. The same shape drives ConvertTo16KHzMonoWav_TrimsLeadingAndTrailingSilence, whose 1.0/0.5/1.0 s variant asserts [0.7, 1.2] s.
materialized.synthesisNotes: Speech samples are trunc(sin * 0.5 * 32768) = trunc(sin * 16384). SilenceTrimmerTests feeds float arrays directly and never goes through PCM16, so the 32768 scaling is the inverse of WavPcmReader's int16/32768 conversion; the round trip reproduces the intended float amplitude to within 1 LSB (3.05e-5), four orders of magnitude below the 0.005 threshold under test.
materialized.notCovered: The quiet-speech half of this entry's expected text has no sample content here; see the separate wav-silence-quietspeech-silence entry.

fixtures.expected: Quiet speech below the retired fixed 0.01 threshold but above the noise floor is not cut by the adaptive threshold.

materialized.format: canonical 44-byte-header RIFF/WAVE PCM16: audioFormat=1, channels=1, sampleRate=16000, bitsPerSample=16, blockAlign=2, byteRate=32000, 25600 frames (1.600 s); 0.3 s exact zeros + 1.0 s of 440 Hz tone at amplitude 0.005 + 0.3 s exact zeros
materialized.expectedOutcome: Per Trim_QuietSpeech_BelowFixedThreshold_IsNotCut (read, NOT executed): the result is non-empty and trimming keeps samples [800, 24800) = 24000 samples = 1.500 s; the C# test asserts [1.0, 1.8] s. SilenceTrimmerTests.QuietSpeech is Tone(seconds, 0.005f), whose peak float amplitude of 0.005 becomes int16 163 here.
materialized.synthesisNotes: Samples are trunc(sin * 0.005 * 32768) = trunc(sin * 163.84), so the peak is 163 and reads back as 163/32768 = 0.004974 - still below the retired 0.01 fixed threshold (FallbackThreshold is 0.005) and far above SilenceTrimmer.AbsoluteFloor of 1e-6, which is the property under test.
materialized.notCovered: Added while materializing wav-silence-speech-silence, whose expected text names quiet speech but whose samples do not contain it. Not one of the four ids requested by the Phase 2 task; drop this entry if unwanted.

fixtures.expected: Two speech phrases separated by long silence remain present and the gap is compressed.

materialized.format: canonical 44-byte-header RIFF/WAVE PCM16: audioFormat=1, channels=1, sampleRate=16000, bitsPerSample=16, blockAlign=2, byteRate=32000, 272000 frames (17.000 s); 5 s exact zeros + 1.0 s of 440 Hz tone at amplitude 0.5 + 5 s exact zeros + the same 1.0 s tone + 5 s exact zeros
materialized.expectedOutcome: Per Trim_LongInternalPause_KeepsBothPhrasesAndCompressesGap (read, NOT executed): the kept window is samples [76000, 196000); the 5 s internal pause exceeds MaxSilenceSeconds 0.6 and is compressed to the 0.3 s GapSilenceSeconds, leaving 4000 + 16000 + 4800 + 16000 + 4000 = 44800 samples = exactly 2.800 s. The C# test asserts [2.4, 3.2] s, and Trim_LongInternalPause_DoesNotContainTheLongPause requires under 4.0 s.
materialized.synthesisNotes: Phase restarts at 0 for each phrase, exactly like SilenceTrimmerTests.Tone, so the two speech segments are byte-identical and a diff of the two phrases is empty. Same 0.5 * 32768 = 16384 scaling as wav-silence-speech-silence.
materialized.notCovered: The 0.2/1.0/5.0/1.0/0.2 s variant of Trim_LongInternalPause_DoesNotContainTheLongPause has no file; it differs from this one only in the outer silence lengths and is trivial to derive from the same generator.

fixtures.expected: Strict PCM16 mono 16 kHz parser handles chunk padding/LIST metadata and rejects invalid formats.

materialized.format: non-canonical RIFF/WAVE: RIFF size 58 covering the full 66 bytes; chunk order LIST(4, 'INFO') at offset 12, then fmt (16, audioFormat=1, channels=1, sampleRate=16000, bitsPerSample=16, blockAlign=2) at 24, then data(2, single sample -16384) at 48, then 8 trailing zero bytes at 58 that a chunk walker reads as one zero-size chunk with a zero id. fmt  arrives after LIST instead of first.
materialized.expectedOutcome: Per To16KHzMonoFloats_ParsesNonCanonicalChunks (read, NOT executed): WavPcmReader walks all chunks, accepts audioFormat=1/channels=1/16000 Hz/16-bit, and returns exactly one float, -0.5. Reproduced byte for byte from the C# test's MemoryStream writes, including the trailing zeros.
materialized.synthesisNotes: Reproduced byte for byte from the C# test's MemoryStream writes, including the 8 bytes it leaves past data. What makes the file non-canonical is the metadata chunk before fmt  and the zero-id zero-size trailer, not a wrong RIFF size: 58 + 8 == 66, so the container is self-consistent and a strict parser must simply skip what it does not recognize.
materialized.notCovered: The LIST chunk here has an even size of 4, so the chunkSize & 1 padding rule is not exercised; see wav-noncanonical-oddpad-chunk. The two rejection cases have their own entries: wav-reject-stereo and wav-reject-nonpcm-format28.

fixtures.expected: The chunk cursor steps by 8 + size + (size & 1), so a 3-byte chunk consumes one pad byte; the pad must be present before the next chunk both at the head and at the tail of the file.

materialized.format: non-canonical RIFF/WAVE: RIFF size 68 covering the full 76 bytes; JUNK(3, 'abc' at 12 plus a pad byte at 23), fmt (16, audioFormat=1, channels=1, sampleRate=16000, bitsPerSample=16) at 24, data(8, samples 32767, -32768, 0, 16384) at 48, then a trailing JUNK(3, 0x010203 at 64 plus a pad byte at 75). Both odd-sized chunks force the word-alignment rule.
materialized.expectedOutcome: Per the cursor arithmetic in WavPcmReader.To16KHzMonoFloats (read, NOT executed): the parser skips both pad bytes and returns four floats, 0.99996948, -1.0, 0.0, 0.5, matching To16KHzMonoFloats_ConvertsPlusMinusFullScale. A parser that forgets the (size & 1) term lands on the wrong chunk and fails.
materialized.synthesisNotes: Data samples are the full-scale quadruple of To16KHzMonoFloats_ConvertsPlusMinusFullScale, so the same file pins both the padding rule and the int16/32768 conversion.
materialized.notCovered: Added while materializing wav-noncanonical-chunks, whose expected text names chunk padding but whose single chunk is even-sized. Not one of the four ids requested by the Phase 2 task; drop this entry if unwanted.

fixtures.expected: A structurally valid 16 kHz PCM16 WAV with channels=2 is rejected, because WavPcmReader accepts mono only.

materialized.format: negative fixture, canonical 44-byte-header RIFF/WAVE PCM16: audioFormat=1, channels=2, sampleRate=16000, bitsPerSample=16, blockAlign=4, byteRate=64000, data(4, four zero bytes). The container itself is well formed; only the channel count is wrong.
materialized.expectedOutcome: Per To16KHzMonoFloats_RejectsStereo (read, NOT executed): a parser matching the C# reference must throw NotSupportedException with the message 'Требуется моно WAV.' Reproduced byte for byte from the C# test. The file is valid only as a negative case and must never be fed to a transcription path.
materialized.synthesisNotes: tools/verify-migration-fixtures.py honours containerExpectation=reject by asserting the fixture's structural validity and inverting only the audioFormat check, so the negative file is verified rather than skipped.

fixtures.expected: audioFormat=28 (MPEG ADPCM) with a 16-bit sample width is rejected, because WavPcmReader accepts audioFormat=1 only.

materialized.format: negative fixture, canonical 44-byte-header RIFF/WAVE: audioFormat=28 (MPEG ADPCM), channels=1, sampleRate=16000, blockAlign=2, byteRate=32000, bitsPerSample=16, data(4, four zero bytes). The width contradicts the codec on purpose.
materialized.expectedOutcome: Per To16KHzMonoFloats_RejectsNonPcmFormat (read, NOT executed): a parser matching the C# reference must throw NotSupportedException with the message 'Требуется PCM-формат WAV (audioFormat=1).' before the bitsPerSample, channels and sampleRate checks are reached. Reproduced byte for byte from the C# test.
materialized.synthesisNotes: The rejection order is observable: a C++ parser that checks bitsPerSample first, or that only validates 16-bit/mono/16 kHz without the codec field, accepts this file and is observably wrong.
materialized.notCovered: float32 (audioFormat=3) and WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE (0xFFFE) are not pinned as fixtures; only the two rejection cases the C# test file already names.
